findings.defect: The translation sanitizes a strongly abusive insult, weakening the escalating profanity and comic hostility of the argument.
findings.rationale: 병신 is substantially harsher than the neutral English “idiot,” and the source deliberately escalates into explicit profanity.

findings.current: “Hey, watch your language. He’s a year younger than me.”
findings.defect: The draft changes the subject from the person being directly addressed to an unidentified third party, altering who is younger than the speaker.
findings.rationale: The omitted Korean subject is the interlocutor being reprimanded; 나보다 나이도 한 살 어리던데 means that person is one year younger than the speaker.
findings.replacement: “Come on, now. You’re a year younger than me, so watch your language.”
findings.source: 어허, 이 사람이. 나보다 나이도 한 살 어리던데 욕은 하지 말지.

findings.current: Even as they grabbed one another by the collars, the news channel next door was reporting breaking news about mutation Gates or monster waves occurring somewhere in the world.
findings.defect: “The news channel next door” sounds as though the channel occupies a neighboring physical location rather than being an adjacent television channel.
findings.rationale: 옆 채널 means another or adjacent television channel; “the news on the next channel” conveys that naturally.
findings.replacement: Even as they grabbed one another by the collars, the news on the next channel was reporting breaking developments about mutation Gates or monster waves somewhere in the world.
findings.source: 그들이 서로의 멱살을 잡는 그 순간에도, 옆 채널 뉴스에서는 세계 어딘가에서 발생한 변이 게이트나 몬스터 웨이브 속보를 알리고 있었으니까.

findings.current: “Your human race is truly a complete mess.”
findings.defect: The line is stiff and sanitizes the Skeleton King’s blunt, coarse assessment, weakening both his voice and the joke that follows.
findings.rationale: 너희 인간들은 directly addresses “you humans,” while 개판 is a coarse colloquial description of utter disorder rather than the formal-sounding “complete mess.”

findings.current: I looked back and forth between the handkerchief and Song Song, then clicked my tongue.
findings.defect: The draft substitutes clicking the tongue for smacking the lips, changing the narrator’s physical action.
findings.rationale: 입맛을 다시다 describes smacking or licking one’s lips, not clicking one’s tongue.
findings.replacement: I looked back and forth between the handkerchief and Song Song, then smacked my lips.
findings.source: 손수건과 송송이를 번갈아 바라보던 나는 입맛을 다셨다.

findings.current: “You must have had a hard time on the long journey. But…”
findings.defect: The draft turns a deferential expression of appreciation into an observation about presumed hardship, losing Team Leader Choi’s courteous subordinate register.
findings.rationale: 고생하셨습니다 here is a polite acknowledgment of the addressee’s effort, not speculation that the journey was difficult.
findings.replacement: “Thank you for your hard work on such a long trip. But…”

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, but it contains two altered physical/subject actions, several softened register choices, one hierarchy loss, and a few localized English issues.
